newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil stevedores return to work, may strike again.
newsitem.headline: Brazil stevedores return to work, may strike again.

text.p: Striking stevedores throughout Brazil returned to work early Saturday after a planned 24-hour stoppage but the president of the National Stevedores Federation did not rule out the possibility of another strike.
"Members returned to work today but we will need to strike again...It is possible that as of Monday (April 7), all the ports will stop again," Abelardo Fernandes told Reuters by telephone.

Around 85 percent of stevedores in Brazil stopped work on Friday to show support for their colleagues in Santos who are protesting over a ruling allowing workers from steel firm Companhia Siderurgica Paulista (Cosipa) to load and unload at Cosipa's private terminal.
Union members say under federal law only registered and qualified workers should work as stevedores even in private terminals.
Stevedores at Santos began striking on April 2 but also returned to work today at the public terminals as expected, said a spokesman for the Santos port authority.
"All the public terminals are operating normally," the spokesman said.
"We have 11 ships waiting in the bay to dock but only two of those have been delayed because of the strike," he added.
Work was still halted at the Cosipa terminal however, he said.
Union members from across the country are expected to arrive in Santos tomorrow when a decision is likely to be taken whether to hold further strikes, Fernandes said.
